memory_candidates.content: To verify a script guarded by deploy-root-guard.sh (requires a '*/.claude/scripts' parent shape) without running a full deploy-headless.sh against the live .claude/ tree, build a synthetic tree instead: mkdir -p $WORKDIR/.claude/scripts/lib, cp the SUT plus every collaborator script + lib/*.sh it calls, chmod +x, then invoke $WORKDIR/.claude/scripts/<sut>.sh directly. This mirrors the project's own test-orchestrate-*.sh harness sandbox convention and lets you exercise real, unmodified script logic for an ad hoc acceptance check without deploying or risking a slow/wedging full verify-deploy.sh run.

Channel-confusion bug class (a script's own stdout carrying both prose logs and structured data it also emits, or a script consuming a collaborator's 2>&1-merged output as if it were pure data) has two independent directions that both need separate fixes: EMIT (structural exec 3>&1 1>&2 entry-point redirect + fd-3 emit, so no future callee can leak into the data channel) and INGEST (a shared run_capture_stdout-style helper at every collaborator call site that explicitly drops stderr before parsing). Fixing one direction does not subsume the other. The dangerous INGEST shape is a while-read NDJSON loop fed from a 2>&1 capture -- the collaborator can still exit 0 while the loop silently ingests a garbage row, so no error path fires at all.

A per-task cycle/retry budget must be charged at the point work is actually dispatched/consumed, not at the point a plan or composition is merely produced -- otherwise a parse failure or other no-op re-run silently and permanently burns budget for work that never happened. The general fix pattern is idempotent composition: cache the composed result keyed by a monotonic sequence number already available in state (here, dispatch_seq), and on re-entry with that key unchanged, return the cached result verbatim without re-charging. For durability across process restarts, add a second, durable ledger entry alongside the in-session cache so the same guarantee holds across invocations, not just within one.
